facts: For the six months ended June 27, 2026, Mobileye reported revenue of $1.066 billion, up 13% year over year; EyeQ SoC revenue increased $90 million or 10% and SuperVision revenue increased $34 million or 181%, mainly from higher volumes.
Average System Price decreased 1% in the first half, mainly from a higher mix of lower-ASP sales to Chinese OEMs, partly offset by a higher SuperVision mix.

Operating cash flow was $210 million in the first half of 2026 versus $322 million a year earlier; property-and-equipment purchases were $51 million versus $28 million, while cash paid for Mentee Robotics net of cash acquired was $591 million.
Mobileye states cash generated by operations is its primary liquidity source and that it expects 2026 capital expenditures to be higher than 2025 as it invests in next-generation product development.

Mobileye disclosed a manufacturing relationship with STMicroelectronics for EyeQ and an agreement with TSMC to manufacture imaging-radar components and some future EyeQ generations as part of an effort to establish redundancy and better control its supply chain.

The filing says substantially all current revenue is derived from commercially deployed ADAS solutions; advanced Surround ADAS, SuperVision, Chauffeur and Drive solutions are approaching production and are expected over time to change revenue mix.

As of July 15, 2026, approximately 2.4% of employees had been called to Israeli reserve duty; Mobileye said operations had not been materially affected to date but regional conflict remained an uncertainty.

factors.name: financialOperatingMomentum
factors.basis: First-half revenue grew 13% and SuperVision revenue grew 181%, but operating cash flow fell to $210 million from $322 million while capex increased, so growth and cash conversion should be evaluated separately.

factors.name: pricingPower
factors.basis: Average System Price declined 1% in the first half as lower-ASP China OEM mix offset part of the benefit from richer SuperVision mix.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: The 10-Q identifies STMicroelectronics as the established EyeQ partner and a TSMC agreement for imaging-radar components and future EyeQ generations specifically intended to add redundancy and control.

factors.name: capitalAllocation
factors.basis: Mobileye spent $591 million net cash on Mentee, increased first-half capex to $51 million, and expects higher full-year capex while relying primarily on operating cash flow; this creates a source-addressed tradeoff between Physical-AI expansion and cash demands.

factors.name: businessModelExpansion
factors.basis: The filing confirms current revenue remains substantially ADAS-derived while advanced ADAS/AV products approach production, preserving a measurable distinction between the cash-generating base and newer optionality.

risks.risk: First-half operating cash flow declined year over year while capex rose and the Mentee acquisition consumed $591 million net cash, increasing the importance of execution and capital-allocation discipline as new businesses scale.
Lower-ASP China OEM mix reduced Average System Price, which can pressure pricing/mix economics even when unit demand grows.

Regional conflict around Israel remains an operational uncertainty; approximately 2.4% of employees were on reserve duty as of July 15, although the company reported no material operational impact to that date.

contradictions: Revenue and advanced-product volumes show growth, while operating cash flow declined and capital intensity increased; stronger commercial momentum therefore does not by itself establish improving cash economics.

Supply-chain diversification through TSMC improves redundancy, but STMicroelectronics remains a key manufacturing partner, so diversification is incremental rather than evidence of supplier independence.
unknowns: How much of the first-half operating-cash-flow decline is timing versus a durable change in cash conversion.
The production allocation and timing between STMicroelectronics and TSMC for future EyeQ generations.
Whether advanced-product mix can offset lower ASP and higher hardware content sufficiently to improve gross-profit dollars and long-run returns on incremental capital.
Whether regional conflict or reserve-duty levels changed materially after July 15, 2026.
